visit_profile.typical_visit: Drive about an hour from Anchorage to the Knik River base (or 45 minutes to Girdwood), weigh in and brief, then a 1-hour landing tour (about 30 minutes in the air and about 30 minutes on the glacier) or a 2-hour, three-landing tour; activity versions add dogsledding (1.5-2 hours), paddleboarding on a meltwater pool (about 4 hours) or ice climbing (about 4 hours).
visit_profile.hours_outdoors: On a landing tour about 30 minutes standing on the glacier, the rest inside an enclosed helicopter cabin; activity tours spend 1 to 4 hours outdoors on the ice.
visit_profile.seasonal_versions: Landing flights all year; dogsledding May-August; paddleboarding mid-May to mid-September; ice climbing in summer and from mid-December to March; ice-cave tours December-March (Outbound); in winter flights run only in daylight.
visit_profile.shelter_checked: The helicopter cabin is enclosed; the weather is felt during the time on the glacier. Outbound: 'Dress in layers for changing weather'. AHT pilots fly only in conditions they judge safe (visibility, wind, icing).
visit_profile.view_dependent: the flight over the Knik Glacier ice field and the Chugach is half of what is sold; low cloud hides it and can stop the landing

view_product_note: A scenic flight and landing: visibility, low cloud and wind on the day decide whether the helicopter flies and how much of the glacier you see.

factor_weights.factor: visibility, low cloud and wind on the day
factor_weights.why: Weather-gated flight: Alpine Air lists 'high winds, fog, low clouds or icing' as causes of delays or cancellations; AHT may reschedule when visibility is low and stops for winds over 30 kt or gust spreads of 15 kt. Low cloud also hides the ice field the flight is sold on. This holds in every month.

factor_weights.factor: which glacier tours run in the season
factor_weights.why: Landing flights run all year, but dogsledding runs only May-August, paddleboarding mid-May to mid-September, ice-cave tours December-March, and winter ice climbing mid-December to March (operators' own pages).

factor_weights.factor: what the glacier looks like: meltwater pools, snow, fall color
factor_weights.why: Blue meltwater pools open from late spring through summer (Alaska.org, Outbound-sponsored); the glacier is under snow in winter; Southcentral Alaska's fall colors peak in September (Travel Alaska).

A landing tour lasts about an hour and activity tours up to four, so daylight binds in winter: AHT flies only in daylight hours then, and the Knik River has 5 h 25 min of daylight in mid-December against 19 h 26 min in mid-June (computed), which narrows the choice of flight times from November to February.

factor_weights.factor: temperature and rain on the ice
factor_weights.why: What to wear for 30 minutes to 4 hours on the glacier: Palmer average highs 66-68°F in June and July, 22-25°F in December and January; rain becomes more frequent from July to September (14.3 wet days in August).
About 88% of Alaska's visitors in 2024-25 came in the summer season (May-September); fewer than 400,000 came from October to April (statewide proxy, not helicopter passengers).

seasonal_archetype_evidence: Two travelers with different priorities choose different halves of the year: summer (mid-May to August) for dogsledding, paddleboarding, blue meltwater pools and long days; December to March for a snow-covered glacier and ice-cave tours; September for fall color. Landing flights run in every month. A first-trip best overall period exists (mid-May to August, because every tour runs), but it is one recommendation among several.
